data.title: B1 Level Check
data.description: A mixed grammar check to estimate whether the learner is working securely at CEFR B1 level.

sections.explain: Present perfect is 'have/has' + past participle: 'have finished'. 'have finish' lacks the participle, and 'am finished' uses the wrong auxiliary.

words.word: I have already finish my homework.
I have already finished my homework.
I am already finished my homework.

sections.explain: Use 'a few' with countable plural nouns like 'people': 'a few people'. 'A little' is for uncountables, and 'few of people' needs 'the'.

words.word: There were only a little people at the party.
There were only a few people at the party.
There were only few of people at the party.

sections.explain: The adjective 'good' takes 'at' for skills: 'good at chess'. 'good in/on' are not the correct collocations.

words.word: She is very good in chess.
She is very good at chess.
She is very good on chess.

sections.explain: This double-comparative structure needs 'the' before each comparative: 'The more ..., the better ...'. 'the more better' doubles the comparative, and omitting 'the' is wrong.

words.word: The more you practise, the better you get.
More you practise, better you get.
The more you practise, the more better you get.

sections.explain: After 'want', use object + to-infinitive: 'want me to study'. English doesn't use 'want that ...', and 'to' is required.

words.word: My parents want me to study medicine.
My parents want me study medicine.
My parents want that I study medicine.

sections.explain: The second conditional uses past simple in the if-clause and 'would' in the result: 'If I won ..., I would travel'. Don't use present 'win' or future 'will' here.

words.word: If I won the lottery, I would travel the world.
If I win the lottery, I would travel the world.
If I won the lottery, I will travel the world.

sections.explain: The present passive is 'is/are' + past participle: 'is spoken'. 'is speaking' is active continuous, and 'English speaks' is active.

words.word: English is spoken all over the world.
English speaks all over the world.
English is speaking all over the world.

sections.explain: In reported speech the tense usually shifts back: 'is' becomes 'was'. Also we say 'told me' but 'said' without an object.

words.word: He said that he is tired.
He said me that he was tired.
He said that he was tired.

sections.explain: For things, use 'that' (or 'which') in a defining relative clause: 'the house that Jack built'. 'what' is never a relative pronoun here, and 'who' is only for people.

words.word: This is the house what Jack built.
This is the house that Jack built.
This is the house who Jack built.

sections.explain: 'Run into' means to meet someone by chance: 'ran into an old friend'. 'run in' and 'run onto' are not correct for this meaning.

words.word: I ran onto an old friend yesterday.
I ran in an old friend yesterday.
I ran into an old friend yesterday.
